title: PR reviewer instructions and CLAUDE.md: block a case fix or workaround that resolving the root cause would make useless; a Root cause not fixed: line ends with #follow_up and the full link
body:
Carries out approval-walk open-decisions-unpushed-branches-memory-claude-md-root-cause-and-cold-read-2026-10-14 items 26.2 and 26.3 (the follow-up link part), with item 34 questions 9 and 12 applied. Walk-minutes: nedlern@ned-box:/home/nedlern/agents/cold-read-improvement/docs/walk/open-decisions-unpushed-branches-memory-claude-md-root-cause-and-cold-read-2026-10-14-minutes.md.

## What changes

- `docs/agents/pr-reviewer-instructions.md`, section "A pull request that fixes a defect": the sentence "If a `Root cause:` line names no root cause, or one the change does not remove, say so in a finding that does not block." becomes item 26.2's rule. A cause the reviewer can show is still in the code blocks. A case fix or workaround still needed after the cause is resolved merges with a `Root cause not fixed:` line ending `#follow_up` and the full link to the follow-up; one that resolving the cause would make useless blocks until it is dropped and the cause resolved. An unknown cause needs `#follow_up` and a link to an issue that looks for it. An outage fix may merge with its follow-up.
- `CLAUDE.md`, root-cause bullet: "if you fix only the case, say why, and what the root cause is or that you could not find it." becomes the matching author-side text.
- The "Review scope" section and CLAUDE.md's copy of it are untouched; `scripts/pr-reviewer-instructions-copies-test.py` passes.

User's words: item 26.2 "Y - assuming this has been fast cold-read" (2026-10-16); item 26.3 "Y - if the prompts have been fast cold read" (2026-10-15/16); question 9 "Don't you resolve a problem. remove feels off. Approved assuming a cold read on final prose" (2026-10-18); question 12 "A" (2026-10-19): `Follow-up: <link>` is written `#follow_up <full link>`.

A cold-read-fast-read ran on both changed files (2026-10-19). Three clarifications to the reviewer sentence were applied: "case fix" defined beside "workaround"; a "no" answer keeps the finding blocking until the change is dropped; the outage exception applies to a case fix or workaround whose answer is no.

## Not in this pull request

- Items 25 and 28 (optional `#kind` hashtags right after the colon, and a proven detect-inform-correct check counting as `Root cause:`): their approved text goes only on the reference page `docs/nedschorus-wiki/nedschorus-root-cause-kinds-problem-tree.md`, which is not on main or on any branch yet.
- Item 26.3's two programs (the `#root_cause_follow_up from PR <number>:` comment at merge, and the daily job) and their GHI-MD edits are separate work.

## Overlap

A second pull request from cold-read-improvement changes five style-guide words in CLAUDE.md (item 34 question 5). One of those changes is on the same CLAUDE.md line as this one (the root-cause bullet: "the merge gate refuses..."). This pull request should merge first.

Root cause: the reviewer rule gave only a non-blocking finding for a `Root cause:` line that left the cause in the code, and CLAUDE.md let an author fix only the case by giving a reason, so case fixes merged with the cause still there (PR 1030's timeout; five fixture patches for GHI 639's inherited `GIT_DIR`). The reviewer now blocks while a cause can be shown still in the code, and only a still-needed fix with a `#follow_up` link settles that finding.
